title: marketplace-outreach-hypothesis-testing-ian
body:
Personal scratchpad for a lightweight, hypothesis-driven sync with channel partners (AWS/GCP/Azure) and a short 1:1 with Drew Harper (AWS Partner Eng). Focus: rapid experiments to validate which marketplace boomi moments move trial-->paid. Not polished — quick bulleted thoughts, numbers to confirm, scripts to A/B test, and follow-up tasks.

Context: We see pockets of high trial conversion from pre-configured AMI images but low discoverability in category searches on AWS Marketplace. GCP appears to get higher click-through from partner solution pages but lower post-provisioning retention. Azure CPL (contact point lead) has been asking for clearer onboarding artifacts. Goal of these syncs: align on 3 experiment variants we can run across marketplaces in Q1, identify implementation owners, and agree measurement windows (2–4 weeks).

Keep in mind: this is a working doc for my prep — will turn into an email summary after the meeting.

Notes-to-self style: short, actionable, and measurables.
agenda: (5m) Quick context + 30s recap of recent marketplace metrics
(10m) Share three candidate experiments (one per marketplace + cross-market test)
(8m) Discuss implementation feasibility and tracking (what data hooks exist?)
(5m) Ownership & timelines: who owns provisioning, listing edits, analytics dashboard
(7m) Risks, compliance, and gating checklist (billing, entitlements, terms)
(5m) Quick AOB and agree next steps
hypotheses: H1: Adding a 'Quickstart AMI + 1-click license' experience on AWS Marketplace will increase paid conversion from trial by ~20% within 30 days (because friction is reduced at provisioning).
H2: GCP solution page with a short video walkthrough and two explicit 'Use cases' templates will drive a 15% lift in active daily usage during first 14 days (helps users see value faster).
H3: Azure customers respond best to a pre-populated ARM template plus an inbound onboarding email sequence; adding both will cut time-to-first-inference by half and increase retention at D14 by 12%.
prep_data_points: Azure: ARM template installs small N but D7 retention = 28% (higher than non-template installs)
Top referral sources for marketplace traffic: cloud-partner-blog (34%), paid-ads (18%), partner-webinars (12%)
Existing instrumentation: marketplace sales feed -> billing events in Snowflake (schema ref: marketplace_events_v2).
Missing: no unified event for 'first successful inference' across marketplace onboarding flows. Need to map and standardize.
talking_points: Why experiments over big bet listing rewrites: faster feedback loops, lower engineering cost, can iterate based on signal, and we keep control of rollout through feature flags.
Propose a lightweight experiment triage: A/B test quickstart vs control on a small cohort (10% traffic) for two weeks, then expand if signal holds.
Data needed from each partner: outbound click attribution, provisioning timestamp, billing activation timestamp, and an 'active inference' event we can join on.
Ask for partner-side measurement support: can they surface a daily CSV/BigQuery export for the cohort? If not, set up webhook -> internal ingestion.
Compliance note: confirm whether adding onboarding emails requires additional marketplace approvals or changes to listing terms.
Lower friction ask: can partner teams add a short 'Try Redwood Inference' CTA in their solution listing hero? Provide copy and a 30-min implementation handoff doc.
action_items: Ian: draft two short landing copy variants for AWS hero CTA (quickstart vs guided walkthrough) — due 2025-01-10
Alex: scope telemetry gaps and propose schema for 'first_successful_inference' event; include mapping for AWS/GCP/Azure — due 2025-01-12
Maya: reach out to Azure CPL to confirm support for ARM-template experiment and ask about approval windows — due 2025-01-11
Drew (AWS): confirm whether AWS listing team can enable 10% traffic experiment and share list of required assets — requested by 2025-01-13
All: quick sync next Thurs 30m to lock variants and measurement plan — calendar invite pending
follow_up_emails_draft:
Subject: Quick follow-up and next steps from marketplace experiment sync

Hey Drew / [AWS Listing contact],

Thanks for the sync — appreciated the quick feedback. Per our conversation: we will run a small A/B experiment on the AWS listing (10% quickstart variant vs 90% control) to measure provisioning -> billing conversion over a 14–28 day window. Action items: 1) we will send finalized hero copy and assets by EOD Fri; 2) please confirm whether the listing team can route a 10% cohort and share provisioning timestamps (or a daily export). If we need a webhook ingestion instead, we can stand that up on our side.

I'll loop in Alex and Maya for instrumentation and Azure/GCP coordination. Will follow-up with updated timelines and a one-page runbook.

Thanks,
Ian
meeting_notes_quick: Drew asked about how we plan to attribute multi-touch referrals; we should propose a deterministic join key (email + provisioning id) and fallback heuristics.
Partner engineering is OK to support a small cohort but needs the assets and copy in a week to submit through review.
Agreement to standardize the 'first_successful_inference' event across clouds; Alex to draft schema.
Risks: legal flagged potential phrasing in hero CTA — loop in legal if we use 'free' incorrectly in listing copy.
